_comment: Mutation testing — an AUDIT, not a CI gate.
READ THIS FIRST: `npm run test:mutation` does NOT use this file. It runs
scripts/mutation-run.mjs, which measures ONE module at a time and generates
its own stryker + vitest config per module, because a whole-tree `stryker
run` never gets past the dry run here. That script is where the scope lives
and where a change belongs. This file is the config for a bare
`npx stryker run`, kept in step with it so the two cannot disagree about what
is in scope.
Coverage says a line ran. It does not say the test would have noticed if the
line were wrong. Stryker changes the code (flips a <= to a <, drops a call,
returns an empty string) and reports which changes NO test caught. Those are
the assertions that aren't there.
Scoped to src/lib and server/ on purpose. Both hold logic whose failure is
SILENT. In src/lib a wrong branch is a data defect — the merge engine, the
importers, the view filter, the escaping. In server/ it is a wrong answer to
'may this person read this row' (access.ts, and db.ts where that answer is
turned into SQL), a credential that verifies when it should not
(passwords.ts, csrf.ts, auth.ts), or two machines deleting each other's work
(backupFiles.ts). None of those surfaces as a visible bug in a browser, which
is exactly why a test suite can be large and still not be watching. Components
stay out: mutating one mostly proves that a rendered string changed, which is
what the RTL suite already asserts.
server/ is a GLOB, not a list of the security-critical modules, so whatever is
added there next is audited without anyone remembering to enrol it — the same
reason the architecture map has a gate rather than good intentions. Three
files are excluded by name: server/index.ts and server/desktop/launcher.ts are
process entry points no test boots, and server/desktop/openBrowser.ts hands a
URL to the OS. A module no test exercises reports 100% survival, which is a
fact `npm run test:coverage` already tells you and which, at a few hundred
mutants, buries the findings worth reading.
The run drives vitest.mutation.config.ts rather than vite.config.ts, because
one test in the suite decides pass/fail from wall clock and has to sit this
one out. The reason is written in that file.
Run with `npm run test:mutation`. It takes a long time (each surviving mutant
means re-running the affected tests), which is exactly why it is not in CI —
it is something you do before a release, read, and act on.

ignorePatterns carries four entries that are load-bearing rather than tidiness. '.claude' — Stryker copies the project into a sandbox, and .claude/worktrees/* holds full git checkouts that OTHER live sessions are editing; a file that vanishes between the scan and the copy fails the whole run with 'ENOENT ... copyfile'. Those worktrees are excluded through .git/info/exclude, which Stryker does not read. 'data' is the same hazard, a live SQLite DB with WAL files being written underneath the copy. 'test-results' and 'playwright-report' are a hazard by VOLUME instead: Playwright leaves tens of megabytes of traces there, and the project is copied once per module, so a whole-tree run would move gigabytes for nothing.

dryRunTimeoutMinutes is raised from Stryker's 5-minute default on purpose: the dry run executes the WHOLE suite once per test-runner process, instrumented, and several of those in parallel do not finish in five minutes. The symptom is 'Initial test run timed out!' before a single mutant is tried, which reads like a broken config rather than a budget. It was 30 when the suite was ~2,600 tests; the suite is ~6,800 now, so the budget moved with it rather than being rediscovered the hard way.
